title: Building a Chess Coach — Anant Dole and Asbjorn Steinskog, Take Take Take
talk_summary: Take Take Take built a chess game-review pipeline that runs Stockfish plus a bank of deterministic detectors to extract grounded facts, then uses an LLM only to translate that structured context into English commentary. They close the loop with a continuously-running Claude Code channel (MCP event injection) that triages user-reported bad commentary, edits prompts/detectors, regenerates, self-verifies, and asks a human before opening a PR.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a trusted solver (Stockfish) and a bank of detectors to produce a structured JSON of facts (threats, tactics, plans), then constrain the LLM to only verbalize that context rather than reason from scratch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the LLM's job is only to translate this information uh into English, because we really don't want it to try to figure out too much on its own

takeaways.technique: Detector bank for recurring defect classes
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a lot of detectors that tries to figure out all all of this, the forks, pins, skewers

takeaways.technique: Small scenario suite + LLM-as-judge + SME spot-check
takeaways.what_they_do: Curate ~16 scenarios from real cases by theme, run candidate models through them via a router, judge with an LLM, and have domain experts arbitrate quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have 16 different scenarios that we created ... We use LLM as a judge
takeaways.numbers: 16 scenarios; Gemini Flash ~75%, Claude ~60% with longer latency

takeaways.technique: Latency-tiered model selection by task phase
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a fast flash model for the latency-critical path and reserve slower reasoning models for patient/interactive phases, benchmarking each on the same eval set.
takeaways.numbers: sub-3s target; ~1s time-to-first-token; ~3s end-to-end on Gemini Flash

takeaways.technique: Event-injected long-running triage agent with human gate
takeaways.what_they_do: A persistent agent session receives user-reported failures as injected events, runs a triage skill (scripts to regenerate, edit prompts/detectors), self-verifies, asks the human a clarifying question in Slack, then opens a PR for human merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It runs a commentary triage skill ... verify its own work. And then it will also ask questions back to Slack

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode the investigation procedure as a reusable skill with executable scripts so the agent follows a fixed process (reproduce, inspect, modify prompt/detector, regenerate, verify) instead of improvising.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It runs a commentary triage skill that we created that outlines its process how it should go about to investigate
